svg.text: How a single pixel's clock travels through the panel — ZIGZAG8
One scan-address pair shown (row k & row k+10) — a quarter of the four interleaved sub-rows. Numbers = shift-clock index.
Rounded arrow = a “skip” to the next adjacent physical column, same row. This is the reversed/forward shift within one 8-pixel segment.
Straight arrow = a “jump” to a different physical row (vertical) or to the start of the next segment (curved-diagonal) — never an adjacent cell.
Row k — clocked in reversed column order (7,6,…,0 within each segment).
Row k+10 — clocked in forward column order (0,1,…,7 within each segment).
virt (0,0) — the logical top-left pixel — lands on DMA col 7 of Row k, which is also clk 0: the very first pixel shifted into the chain.
Rows k and k+10 are physically 10 rows apart (drawn adjacent for clarity). The identical pattern repeats for row k+20/k+30 (RGB2 lane) and for all 10 scan addresses, clocks 0–159.
